literature_notes: All five ledger lines (L1–L5) describe a single CRISPR/Cas9 HDR knock-in of a DDDDK (FLAG-like) tag into exon 2 of the COL17A1 gene in HaCaT keratinocytes. COL17A1 is a type II transmembrane collagen: its N-terminus (residues 1–466) is intracellular, the TM domain spans 467–487, and the ectodomain runs 488–1497. Exon 2 of COL17A1 encodes sequence in the early N-terminal intracellular region (approximately residues 14–60 based on the published 56-exon gene structure of NM_000494). The DDDDK tag therefore sits on the cytoplasmic face and is used in the paper for immunoprecipitation from cell lysates and co-IP of the integrin α6/β4 complex — applications that require intracellular, not surface, access. No ledger line reports any insertion in the extracellular domain (488–1497) of full-length, membrane-anchored COL17A1. The ledger contains no evidence for a surface-accessible epitope tag site; zero sites is the correct answer.

literature_other_positions.note: DDDDK tag inserted in-frame into exon 2 of COL17A1 by CRISPR/Cas9 HDR; exon 2 encodes the early N-terminal intracellular domain (~residues 14–60), which is cytoplasmic (topology: intracellular 1–466); used for immunoprecipitation from cell lysates, not surface labelling.
